issues.legal_issue: A preliminary decree that conclusively adjudicates rights is a final decision on the matters it determines, even when further proceedings are required to obtain executable relief.
material_facts: An Official Receiver sold joint-family property, including the interests of the insolvent father's sons.
In a partition suit, the court held that the Official Receiver lacked authority to sell the sons' interests and passed a preliminary decree in their favour.
The preliminary decree was affirmed on appeal and was not challenged further, although proceedings to obtain a final decree remained pending when the amending law came into force.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary decree was a final decision, as to the matters it determined, within the meaning of the saving proviso. The earlier sale was therefore protected from the effect of the amending law, and the sons were entitled to a final decree.
issues.legal_principle: Under the first proviso to s. 28A of the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920, as inserted by the Provincial Insolvency (Amendment) Act, 1948, an earlier transfer by a court or receiver is saved if it has been the subject of a final decision by a competent court. A decision is final when it would operate as res judicata between the parties unless altered through an appeal, revision, or review permitted by law. A preliminary decree is conclusive as to the matters it determines; its finality does not depend on whether it is executable or whether further proceedings are needed to obtain relief. Section 97 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 supports that conclusion by precluding a party who did not appeal a preliminary decree from disputing its correctness in an appeal from the final decree. In re A Debtor, [1929] 2 Ch. 146, was distinguished on its facts; Vakalapudi Sri Ranga Rao v. Mutyala Ammanna was distinguished because it concerned interlocutory remand orders, not a preliminary decree.

predicates.suit_with_preliminary_and_final_decree_s: The proceeding is a kind of suit in which the court may decide the parties' rights by a preliminary decree and later issue a final decree.
predicates.preliminary_decree_adjudicates_disputed_: The court determines disputed rights between the parties in the preliminary decree.
predicates.preliminary_decree_remains_unaltered: The preliminary decree has not been reversed or modified through a permitted challenge.

issues.definition: When a suit has preliminary and final decree stages, the preliminary decree determines disputed rights, and it remains unaltered, those rights are treated as conclusively decided.
